world.h: Iran says Hormuz will 'never return' to pre-war status
world.b: Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the strait is governed by the laws of the two states bordering it, and that Iran sent its seven conditions for talks to the US through a Qatari mediator and awaits a reply.
world.title: Hormuz Strait will ‘never return’ to pre-war status, Iran’s Ghalibaf says

world.h: Russia's ambassador to the US dies suddenly
world.b: Moscow announced the death of Alexander Darchiev, its envoy to Washington since last March and a specialist in Russia-US relations, without giving details.
world.title: Moscow announces sudden death of Russia’s envoy to US

world.h: Russia-Ukraine talks end with deal on prisoner swap
world.b: US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange, expected within weeks. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will brief Putin in Moscow, then meet Zelenskyy in Dublin.

world.h: Iran's chief negotiator says Tehran awaits US decision on latest proposal
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage of the US-Israel war on Iran.
world.title: Iran chief negotiator says waiting for US decision on latest proposal

world.h: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz stays shut
world.b: Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei called reports of negotiations or a meeting in Qatar "a pure lie" and said the Strait of Hormuz won't reopen until the US meets Tehran's seven conditions. Trump said new attacks on Iran were unnecessary.

world.h: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000
world.b: The outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain has now infected more than 11,000 people and killed 5,387, the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. No vaccine or treatment exists for the strain, and eight of 26 provinces are affected.

world.h: Probe suggests Alaska gas project may serve Russian intel
world.b: A ProPublica investigation found surveyors linked to Russian gas giant Novatek worked off Alaska's sensitive North Slope in 2025 and this year. An expert called such Russia-backed information gathering near US shores a direct challenge to sovereignty and security.
world.title: A Natural Gas Project Off Alaska’s Coast May Be a Russian Ploy for Intel on the Arctic

world.h: US skips UN human rights review for second year
world.b: The United States left an empty chair at the UN's universal periodic review in Geneva for a second straight year, the only member state ever to do so. The ACLU told journalists the administration continues to violate human rights.

world.h: Russia, Ukraine and US negotiators meet in Abu Dhabi
world.b: The talks are the first three-way round since February, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mediating. European foreign ministers pressed Secretary of State Marco Rubio for a seat at the table.

national.h: Bessent moves to military base over safety concerns
national.b: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after media reports helped identify his home address, as he leads a sweeping financial campaign against Iran and US intelligence shows Tehran stepping up efforts to target Americans, the AP reported.
national.title: AP report: Bessent moves to a military base over safety concerns

national.h: SS United States to become a reef off Florida
national.b: The historic ocean liner, which still holds the trans-Atlantic speed record from its 1952 maiden voyage, was set to be intentionally sunk off the Florida panhandle Wednesday.
national.title: WATCH LIVE: SS United States, once world’s fastest ocean liner, sinks to become reef off Florida

national.b: Keach, known for playing detective Mike Hammer, Frank James in 'The Long Riders' and Hamlet on stage, died at his family's home in Poland after a long battle with heart failure, his wife said.
national.title: Actor Stacy Keach, who played a private eye and plenty more, dies at 85

national.h: Kennedy family sues to block Trump's arch
national.b: Nine Kennedy relatives filed a federal lawsuit to stop the proposed 250-foot arch, saying it would cast a shadow over gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery, including JFK's Eternal Flame.
national.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave

national.h: AI-voiced hoax calls are fooling 911 dispatchers
national.b: Swatting calls made with AI-generated voices, like a bomb threat that closed a Yuba County, California, high school in August, are getting harder for emergency dispatchers to detect.

national.h: Veterans hospital in crisis after VA cuts
national.b: A ProPublica investigation finds the VA hospital in East Orange, New Jersey, struggling after the administration's dismantling of the VA, including an operating room closed by a broken ventilation system and short-staffed repair crews.
national.title: Trump Promised to Care for America’s Veterans. The VA Is Now “Collapsing From the Inside.”

national.h: Three charged in Iran-backed terror plots
national.b: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan accused three men of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted nearly 20 attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the US, plus a planned assault on RAF Fairford in Britain. Only one is in custody.

national.h: Door-to-door shots slow measles in Amish country
national.b: In Chester County, Pennsylvania, health department supervisor Dale Weiser has spent months driving to Amish homes to vaccinate families against measles. Word of mouth has spread her phone number through the community almost as fast as the virus.

politics.h: Trump's $10 billion BBC defamation suit can proceed
politics.b: A federal judge in Florida let Trump's defamation claim over a BBC documentary move forward without ruling on its merits, but dismissed a claim under the state's unfair business practices law.
politics.title: Judge allows Trump defamation case against BBC to proceed but tosses 1 claim

politics.h: Peltola campaign sues over rejected Alaska ballots
politics.b: A state judge promised a swift ruling on Mary Peltola's lawsuit seeking the list of rejected absentee voters in her close Senate race against Republican Dan Sullivan. The state says releasing it would violate voter privacy.

politics.h: White House warns Democrats against investigations
politics.b: White House counsel Will Scharf wrote to Rep. Robert Garcia, likely the next House Oversight chair, suggesting planned probes of the administration may amount to "blatant criminality." Garcia had told Trump officials to "lawyer up."

politics.h: Critics slam DOJ moves to erase Trump allies' convictions
politics.b: The Justice Department asked a court to drop Steve Bannon's contempt of Congress conviction, which an appeals court upheld, and Bannon's lawyers don't object. Legal experts say it fits a pattern of unopposed dismissals for Trump allies.

The House voted 211-204 to send Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, short-circuiting a floor vote that could have come as early as Wednesday.

politics.h: Sanders, Slotkin won't back Schumer as leader
politics.b: Sen. Bernie Sanders said he will not support Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader in the new Congress, joined by Michigan's Elissa Slotkin in calling for a new generation of leadership. Several incoming Democratic senators have echoed the call.

politics.h: Senate Republicans keep Thune as leader
politics.b: Senate Republicans reelected John Thune, unopposed, as their leader after three tense meetings over midterm losses that cost them at least seven seats. Wisconsin's Ron Johnson, who pushed to delay the vote, walked out as voting began.

The Senate moved forward a bill that would speed permitting for clean and fossil fuel energy projects, shorten environmental reviews, limit court challenges and make data center owners pay for the power infrastructure they need. Trump urged lawmakers to back it.

At his first Pentagon press conference in nearly six months, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution "a stunt" and "sabotage," framing criticism of the Iran war as policy disagreements. The House may hold a procedural vote on the resolution Tuesday.

politics.h: House Republicans pick Jim Jordan as minority leader
politics.b: Ohio's Jim Jordan beat Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot to lead House Republicans in the next Congress. The Freedom Caucus co-founder inherits a historically small conference after last week's midterm losses and warned of coming Democratic oversight.

international.h: More than a million in Lebanon face acute hunger
international.b: A joint UN and Lebanese agriculture ministry statement warned the number is expected to rise to 1.15 million by mid-2027 as savings run out and food and fuel costs strain households.
international.title: More than one million people in Lebanon face acute food shortages, UN says

international.h: Tens of thousands join Poland's nationalist march
international.b: Marchers filled Warsaw for the annual Independence Day march, long criticized for anti-Semitic and anti-immigration rhetoric, which supporters call an expression of national pride.
international.title: Tens of thousands join Poland’s nationalist Independence Day march

international.h: Storm Charles shuts Portugal's schools and grounds flights
international.b: Portugal canceled more than 300 flights and about 8,000 schools closed as the Atlantic storm brought gusts above 120km/h. Lisbon streets flooded as people stayed home on government advice.
international.title: Portugal cancels more than 300 flights, shuts schools due to Storm Charles

international.h: Rights group raises alarm over jailed Gaza doctor
international.b: Physicians for Human Rights Israel says a review of Dr. Hussam Abu Safia's records shows a 14kg weight loss in four months and untreated chest pain, and is petitioning to free 14 Gaza doctors held without charge.

international.h: Hundreds of Italian schools evacuated over email bomb threats
international.b: Schools across Italy were evacuated after emailed bomb alerts that also threatened Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. The same purported author claimed earlier threats to newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria, amid wider worry about hybrid attacks in Europe.

international.h: Spain's first general strike in 14 years targets housing crisis
international.b: Millions of workers walked off the job to demand action on housing, slowing transit in Barcelona and Madrid and closing many schools, less than three weeks before a national election.

international.h: Yemeni government forces and Houthis trade heavy attacks
international.b: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces said they hit Houthi positions in six governorates with air strikes, drones and artillery, claiming about 190 fighters killed or injured. Al Jazeera could not verify the claims.

international.h: Russia says it downed 146 drones over Leningrad region
international.b: Russia claimed to intercept 146 drones over the Leningrad region, where a drone attack sparked a fire at Ust-Luga port. The strikes came as US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi entered their final day, which Zelenskyy called constructive.

international.h: Former Iraqi lawmaker found dead in Beirut
international.b: Ahmed al-Alwani's body was found in an apartment in Beirut's Tariq al-Jdideh neighbourhood. His office called it an assassination, and Lebanon's top prosecutor is overseeing the investigation.

international.h: Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza's Rafah crossing
international.b: The Ferrari driver toured the Rafah border crossing with North Sinai's governor, greeting Egyptian Red Crescent staff and asking how often aid can enter Gaza.

international.h: David Walliams accused of grooming young women
international.b: An ITV News and Guardian investigation accused the children's author and former 'Little Britain' star of grooming. Walliams denied being a predator or breaking the law, and the BBC is reviewing all material featuring him.

international.h: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat
international.b: Russia expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Moldova's expulsion of a Russian embassy employee in October, after Moldova said a Russian drone carrying explosives crashed near homes and an energy facility.

international.h: UN peacekeepers come under fire in southern Lebanon
international.b: A UNIFIL patrol was shot at in southern Lebanon and returned fire. No casualties were reported, and the mission called for an investigation, warning that deliberate attacks on peacekeepers violate international law.

international.h: Rwanda genocide suspect deported from US to face trial
international.b: Jean Léonard Teganya, indicted in 2014 over alleged genocide crimes in Huye district, arrived in Rwanda Monday after deportation from the United States and is being questioned by police before prosecutors take his case.

international.h: US soldier arrested in Britain on Russia spying suspicion
international.b: Counterterror police arrested a 41-year-old US soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, working with the FBI and US military. FBI Director Kash Patel called it an important arrest.

international.h: Israel's president urges compromise as new Knesset sworn in
international.b: Israel's president urged lawmakers to make concessions and avoid a repeat election as the 26th Knesset was sworn in. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming a government, has 28 days to build a coalition.

international.h: Egypt train crash fuels calls for accountability
international.b: Parliament's transport committee summoned the transport minister after a Giza-Fayoum train rammed another on the Cairo-Aswan line Sunday in al-Ayyat district. Opposition voices are demanding resignations as the crash questions years of railway upgrades.

international.h: Indonesia's vice president offers to resign
international.b: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, offered to resign in a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto amid questions over his academic documents. It was not clear whether Prabowo accepted.

international.h: Spain weighs suspending TikTok over abuse videos
international.b: Spain is considering suspending TikTok after the nonprofit Maldita.es found more than 1,000 child sexual abuse videos with 48 million views and over 20,000 suspected predator profiles during 35 days of monitoring.

international.h: Fog pile-up kills at least 12 in Bulgaria
international.b: About 50 cars and trucks crashed in thick fog on the motorway near Yambol linking Sofia and Burgas, killing at least 12 and sending 46 to hospital. Prime Minister Rumen Radev called it a tragedy.

international.h: Three workers die at Tata iPhone parts plant
international.b: Three contract workers died after inhaling gas while cleaning an effluent treatment tank at a Tata Electronics site in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, late Monday. Tata handles roughly 40% of iPhone assembly in India.

international.h: US moves aircraft from second UK base over Iran threat
international.b: US refuelling tankers at RAF Mildenhall in eastern England were diverted to Germany and elsewhere Monday after a threat from Iran, The Wall Street Journal reported. Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath were raised to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest threat level.

international.h: Europe presses Rubio for a seat at Ukraine talks
international.b: Meeting in Paris with G7 counterparts, European foreign ministers told Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Europe must have a say in any deal to end Russia's war on Ukraine, as US-mediated talks began in Abu Dhabi. Germany's Johann Wadephul rejected any fundamental change to Europe's security architecture.

international.h: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in West Bank raid
international.b: Moataz Iyad Daghlas was shot in the village of Burqa near Nablus, and two other teens were wounded. Israel's military said soldiers fired to stop stone-throwing.

international.h: Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired at Riyadh
international.b: A Saudi-led coalition spokesperson blamed the Houthis after two ballistic missiles and a cruise missile were intercepted, following an attack on a key pipeline.

international.h: Cameroon sets Feb. 7 date for twice-delayed elections
international.b: President Paul Biya, 93, announced the legislative and local vote by decree as authorities crack down on the opposition a year after his disputed reelection.

business.b: The biggest US oil company signed a nonbinding memorandum with Venezuela's government and PDVSA to evaluate exploration and production, nearly two decades after leaving and months after its CEO called the country "uninvestable."

business.h: Blacklisted Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips
business.b: Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 AI chips through a third party despite US export restrictions, procurement records reviewed by Reuters show. The school also rented access to the chips this year.

business.h: IBM Consulting ends most US foreign worker sponsorships
business.b: IBM's biggest division, with more than 150,000 employees, will end most sponsorships of foreign workers in the US, saying its use of high-skilled visa programs had been declining for years. The move comes amid Trump administration pressure on H-1B use.

business.h: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in IPO
business.b: Anthropic's SEC filing plans 825 million shares priced at $70 to $78, valuing the AI company at up to $1.4 trillion, plus a $26 billion private placement backed by Google, Nvidia, Microsoft and AMD. The valuation is below earlier estimates amid worries over AI spending.

business.h: New car prices hit a record above $51,000
business.b: The average transaction price for a new vehicle reached $51,109, Kelley Blue Book reported, about $500 above the previous record. The 2.1% yearly rise is below inflation, as tariffs and demand for larger vehicles keep prices high.

business.h: Inflation runs hotter than expected in October
business.b: Consumer prices rose 0.4% from September to October and core prices rose 0.3%, both a tenth of a point above forecasts, the Labor Department said. At an annual rate both are well above the Fed's 2% target.

business.h: Gates holds $29 billion stake in landfill giant
business.b: A ProPublica investigation finds Bill Gates owns 38% of Republic Services, America's No. 2 landfill operator. EPA inspectors have repeatedly found methane escaping Republic landfills above federal limits, and the company has lobbied against rules that would make the waste industry cleaner.
business.title: The Garbage Man: Bill Gates Has Earned Billions Investing in Climate-Polluting Landfills

science.h: 'Climate crisis is outrunning us,' Guterres tells COP31
science.b: Opening leaders' talks in Antalya, the UN chief said the last four years were the hottest on record and called for fossil fuels to "go the way of the dinosaurs," warning that fossil fuel interests keep profiting while the planet suffers.

Climate activist Greta Thunberg criticized the COP31 talks co-hosted by Turkiye and Australia, saying negotiations are filled with fossil fuel lobbyists and that "everything and everyone we love is at stake."

science.h: Iran war oil shock trims global CO2 emissions
science.b: Fossil fuel carbon emissions fell 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2 billion metric tons, the Global Carbon Project found, mostly because the Iran war choked oil through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil emissions dropped nearly 2% while coal rose 0.6%.

sports.h: Kansas routs Kentucky at Champions Classic
sports.b: No. 15 Kansas beat No. 24 Kentucky 89-69 as Tre White scored 30 and Trey Kaufman-Renn added 12 points and six assists, even without injured guard Melvin Council Jr.

sports.h: Michigan State upsets No. 2 Duke at Champions Classic
sports.b: Jeremy Fears Jr. had 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as fifth-ranked Michigan State beat Duke 79-73 at the United Center.

sports.h: Alabama jumps to No. 3 in second CFP rankings
sports.b: Alabama rose two spots to No. 3, the earliest a two-loss team has reached the committee's top four, while Tennessee, which beat the Tide, sits at No. 8. The committee chair cited Alabama's top-ranked strength of schedule.

Minnesota reacquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick ahead of the trade deadline, after Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 Monday. The deal hands Las Vegas's starting job to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza.

sports.h: Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart win Rookie of the Year
sports.b: The Tigers' McGonigle took 28 of 30 first-place votes in the AL, and the Reds' Stewart won in the NL.

sports.h: Jaguars trade for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis
sports.b: Jacksonville sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia on the eve of the trade deadline, after also adding Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux.

sports.h: College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in 2027
sports.b: The new format has 19 at-large bids, four for Power Four champions and one for the top Group of Six champion, and will eliminate conference championship games, CBS Sports reports.

sports.h: Jaguars acquire All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from Falcons
sports.b: Atlanta gets a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Jacksonville is 6-2, and the NFL trade deadline is Tuesday.

goodnews.h: Norway's eider keepers build nests for migrating ducks
goodnews.b: On the Vega Islands, just south of the Arctic Circle, keepers shelter nesting eider ducks each spring and collect their prized down.

goodnews.h: Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient
goodnews.b: Kenya's final Ebola patient has recovered, and the country will be declared disease-free on Dec. 23 if no new cases emerge. Seven of its nine confirmed patients recovered, and there was no community spread.

goodnews.h: Volunteer musicians bring songs to hospitalized veterans
goodnews.b: Volunteers with Musicians On Call play bedside for patients, including in the hospice unit at the DC VA Medical Center, delivering what the nonprofit calls the healing power of music.

goodnews.h: Nations pledge to double rooftop solar by 2030
goodnews.b: At the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, five countries launched the Global Rooftop Solar Declaration, aiming to grow homes with rooftop panels from about 150 million to at least 300 million by 2030.

local.h: East Side's Cinema 123 closes after 60 years
local.b: The Angelika theater near the Queensboro Bridge screened its last film after its building sold to Roger Equities for $41 million, weeks after the Kips Bay AMC announced it will close.
local.title: Manhattan’s East Side loses another movie theater to development

local.h: Teen arrested in killing of Bronx boy walking to school
local.b: Police arrested a 17-year-old in the Oct. 29 shooting death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong near Crotona Park. The motive is not yet clear.
local.title: Teen arrested for fatal shooting of 15-year-old Bronx boy walking to school, NYPD says

local.h: Sanitation supervisors rack up speed camera tickets
local.b: Gothamist found 763 sanitation department cars assigned to supervisors and other staff have collected at least 2,375 speed camera tickets since 2023. Advocates want faster rollout of speed limiters, which Mayor Mamdani supports.
local.title: NYC sanitation supervisors keep speeding on the job, data shows

local.h: Chelsea NYCHA redevelopment splits Mamdani's allies
local.b: Tenant activists at Fulton and Elliott-Chelsea Houses have joined DSA to fight the $1.2 billion plan to replace about 2,000 public housing units with mixed-income development, calling it privatization. Mamdani says a teardown is cheaper than repairs.
local.title: Mamdani’s redevelopment plan for NYCHA complex in Chelsea spills into DSA

local.h: Ninth death in city jail custody this year
local.b: A man held at Rikers' Robert N. Davoren Center was found dead in his bed, at least the ninth death in Department of Correction custody this year. The department did not release a cause and will investigate.
local.title: Rikers detainee's death is at least the 9th in corrections department custody this year

local.h: Hochul keeps door open to redrawing House map
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Democratic gains don't necessarily end the push to amend the state constitution for mid-decade redistricting, which could let Democrats redraw New York's districts as soon as 2028, but she didn't commit.
local.title: Gov. Hochul keeps the door open to redrawing New York’s congressional map

local.h: Man indicted in killing of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors indicted a city Department of Education worker in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on a Bath Beach path. Police say surveillance shows him fleeing the scene.
local.title: Man indicted in stabbing murder of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez

local.h: Judge orders city to answer ICE shelter subpoena
local.b: A federal judge ruled City Hall must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with serious criminal histories. The Mamdani administration says it is evaluating next steps.
local.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC

local.b: The city's Department of Transportation told a community board that concrete work on west Canal Street, planned for this fall, will slip to next year in the Reimagining Canal Street project.
local.title: Manhattan's Canal Street is getting a face-lift, but it'll take a while

local.h: East Harlem buildings head to auction despite City Hall push
local.b: Thirty-eight deteriorating buildings with about 850 mostly rent-stabilized apartments, formerly owned by bankrupt Emerald Equities Group, go to auction starting Tuesday. Mayor Mamdani's administration had backed a bid by affordable housing developer Spatial Equity to buy the portfolio first.
local.title: Rent-stabilized buildings hit auction block, despite Mamdani’s efforts to intervene

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: A 30 percent chance of showers, mainly between 2am and 4am.  Increasing clouds, with a steady temperature around 57. South wind 6 to 9 mph becoming east after midnight.

periods.name: Thursday
periods.text: Showers, mainly after noon.  Steady temperature around 57. East wind 10 to 14 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Rain.  Low around 42. North wind 14 to 18 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 80%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: Rain, mainly before 4pm.  Temperature falling to around 37 by 1pm. North wind 14 to 17 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 90%. New precipitation amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.

periods.name: Friday Night
periods.text: A 30 percent chance of rain, mainly before 7pm.  Mostly cloudy, with a low around 40. Northwest wind around 13 mph.

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: Partly sunny, with a high near 48.

localgood.h: Lost Georgia O'Keeffe painting found in East Village closet
localgood.b: A niece helping her aunt settle her affairs found O'Keeffe's landscape "Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I" in a wooden box behind coats. Christie's specialists called the find exceptional.
localgood.title: Long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting found in East Village closet
